title: Divine Jealousy for Israel
english: He draws the faithful from the nations and the Jews into unity and peace, so that they may not be lifted up in pride, but instead offer their graces to God, who has forgiven their transgressions without remembering wrongs.
He says he desires to glorify his own ministry, not out of vain ambition, but to provoke his own flesh—meaning Israel, his kin according to the flesh—to jealousy.
He speaks as if he were saying that Eucleus, the worthy one, and the most beloved to God of his mission are his, and that those throughout the whole sunlit world are most necessary to him.
He does not seek to appear crowned with garlands for vain or foreign displays of boasting, but only to save his own race according to the flesh.
He accomplishes this as if he were a center of zeal for someone, raising up the necessity to be justified by the grace that comes through Christ.
For if their rejection is the reconciliation of the world, what is their acceptance but life from the dead?
Since Israel could not be praised by faith or by conduct, he has turned to the words of the economy, and he says their unbelief has become a precursor to the world’s proximity to God.
He tries to say that through which they have stumbled, perhaps they also have become benefactors of the world, and as it were, having fallen and lying low, he crowns the Jews.
For life he declares to be from the dead their acceptance, if indeed it is true, as has become their rejection the world’s reconciliation.
If you remain.
Therefore the word is skillfully spoken.
translator_notes: The Greek text appears to be a continuous excerpt from a larger work, likely a homily or treatise, with no clear beginning or end in this chunk. Several clauses are grammatically complete, but the overall flow suggests mid-sentence continuation at both start and end.

The phrase 'Εὐκλεᾶ τε καὶ ἀξιόχρεων καὶ φιλαιτάτην Θεῷ τὴν ἀποστολὴν τὴν ἐμὴν' is syntactically irregular and may reflect editorial corruption or a quoted source; it is translated literally as preserved.
The numeral '242' in [p8] is clearly a folio or line number from the source manuscript and not part of the argument; it has been omitted from translation.

The final fragment 'Εὐτέχνως ἄρα ὁ λόγος' is grammatically incomplete, lacking a verb or predicate; it is rendered as 'Therefore the word is skillfully spoken' to preserve the intended sense while acknowledging the ellipsis.
No invented words or clauses have been added; all translations reflect the source text exactly as given, with edge cuts noted but not completed.

title: Salvation of Israel and the Gentiles
english: The apostle was made aware that Israel, having sinned against what is proper, is restored through faith in Christ, and is exhorted towards what is beneficial, and to lay claim to its own root through faith in Christ.
The Gentiles, on the other hand, are glorified by God and exhorted to steadfastness in faith and piety.
If one remains faithful, one remains a noble branch of the holy root, but if one disobeys, one will also be cut off from the root.
This will continue until the fullness of the Gentiles enters, and thus all Israel will be saved.

However, if many Gentiles have died in unbelief, how can it be said that the fullness of the Gentiles has entered, and not all Israel will be saved, since the Jews will receive the son of lawlessness, having been unmindful of the love for Christ?
The Lord himself said, 'I came in my Father's name, and you did not accept me; if another comes in his own name, you will accept him.' (John 5:43)
And the wise Paul said, 'They did not accept the love for the truth so as to be saved.' (2 Thessalonians 2:10)
God sends a working of error to those who have rejected the truth, leading them to believe the lie, which is a working of delusion.
In response to this, we must consider again and examine that God's plan, which proposes the gift of faith to all people without exception, has been extended to all.
If some have willingly fallen away and sinned against this gift, it does not mean that God's word is false.

Rather, it is a testament to the fact that God's kindness and gentleness have been extended to all, including the fullness of the Gentiles, who have come to know the mind and purpose of the one who called them.
The fullness of the Gentiles has come in, and all Israel will be saved, as it is written in Scripture, for that which is to be saved will be saved in due time.
It is confirmed that Israel will be saved, and this is a promise that gives us hope.
The Redeemer will come from Zion (Isaiah 59:20).
Israel was called by God at specific times through the prophet Moses, and as a result, they were delivered from their affliction in Egypt.
In contrast, the servants of demons, referring to the pagan nations, were not recipients of this divine call and deliverance.

title: Universal Mercy
english: The Egyptians, as they perceived, disobeyed the mercy shown to the Israelites because they did not believe in the divine signs performed through Moses, and they refused to acknowledge the God of the Hebrews.

The crowd was barely allowed to perform priestly duties in the wilderness of the Jews, and they clung to their ancient deceit, but now they were pitied because Israel, who also disobeyed the mercy of the nations, was overthrown, so that they themselves might be pitied in due time, as Israel had disobeyed the mercy of the nations.

Thus, the transgressions of both parties are equally in need of divine assistance, for it is said that all are enclosed in disobedience by God, so that He may have mercy on all, and this is not considered the work of divine counsel, that some disobey so that they might be pitied when they fall into this.

Rather, having enclosed them in disobedience, God reveals them to be guilty of the transgressions of disobedience, and as it were, convicted by their own actions, which subjects them to wickedness, as if they needed only to be pitied and to be shown mercy.
I know and am convinced in the Lord Jesus that nothing is common or unclean in itself, for when something has come into its own nature, it is sanctified through the word of God and prayer.
We remember that God, having brought all things into being, saw that they were very good and blessed them (Genesis 1:31).

While God is praising and blessing his own creations, who would dare say that they are sources of pollution and uncleanness, and not rather that God makes the confession of the one who brought them into existence?
For all things are pure, but the unbelief of some makes them common, and it is not the things themselves that are considered common, for nothing is common by nature.

Just as for the perfect, the mind is one, the natural God, and there is no other besides him, so too for those who have believed, the things from God are pure and clean, and nothing is common in nature.
The idea that something is common is a product of human judgment, not a property of the thing itself, and nothing is common in itself.

As Christ said, 'it is not what enters into the mouth that defiles the man' (Matthew 15:11), and we know that all food goes into the stomach and is then expelled into the latrine, which is a natural process.
Therefore, nothing that is used for food is common or unclean in its own nature, for it is sanctified through the word of God and prayer.
